evidence.note: CONFIRMED. Probe: grep the Import-linter row of docs/ddflow/research/graph-internal.md. Pre-fix it said '(6 contracts: layers, surfaces-through-api, subprocess-home, fsio-home, digest-home, extras-one-adapter)' and omitted http-home; tests/test_architecture_import_contracts.py CONTRACTS is frozenset of 7 (includes http-home). Single refuter would have been the doc already saying 7 and naming http-home.
r-small-files: test file stays ~140 lines, under 30KB. r-tell-dont-discover: doc row already enumerates contracts; only the count and the missing http-home changed. No new rule violated.

Commit 83b488a3b. graph-internal.md row 12 now lists 7 contracts (added http-home); added regression test test_graph_internal_names_every_contract asserting every CONTRACTS member and '7 contracts' appear in the row (fails pre-fix: http-home absent, '6 contracts' present).

chunk_findings.detail: The count assertion is substring-based: `assert f"{len(CONTRACTS)} contracts" in row`. If `CONTRACTS` has 7 entries and the docs row contains `Import-linter contracts: 17 contracts` (or `27 contracts`, etc.), the assertion passes because `"7 contracts"` is a substring of `"17 contracts"`. The test can therefore pass while the documented contract count is wrong, defeating the count-drift guard it is supposed to provide.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_architecture_import_contracts.py:test_graph_internal_names_every_contract

chunk_findings.detail: The test only checks that every name in `CONTRACTS` appears somewhere in the selected line and that the expected count string appears. It never checks that the line does not name additional contracts. For example, with 7 entries in `CONTRACTS`, a row like `Import-linter contracts: 7 contracts: <all seven names>, stale-contract` satisfies all assertions even though the documentation lists an extra contract and is inconsistent with `CONTRACTS`. Thus it does not fully guard against drift when contracts are added or removed.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_architecture_import_contracts.py:test_graph_internal_names_every_contract

chunk_findings.detail: Both assertions use raw substring membership, so they can pass even when the doc is wrong. For example, if a future row contains `http-home` but omits the separate `http` contract, `assert "http" in row` passes because `http` is a substring of `http-home`; similarly, if the row count is incorrectly written as `17 contracts` while `len(CONTRACTS)` is 7, `assert f"7 contracts" in row` passes because `"7 contracts"` is a substring of `"17 contracts"`. The test therefore does not fully enforce the doc/CONTRACTS drift guarantee it claims.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_architecture_import_contracts.py:134-135

chunk_findings.detail: The count guard is substring-based: with `len(CONTRACTS) == 7`, `assert f"{len(CONTRACTS)} contracts" in row` also matches a docs row that says `17 contracts`, `27 contracts`, etc. For example, if row 12 is changed to `.importlinter (17 contracts: layers, surfaces-through-api, subprocess-home, fsio-home, digest-home, http-home, extras-one-adapter)`, the test still passes because `"7 contracts"` is a substring of `"17 contracts"`, so it does not reliably guard the contract count.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_architecture_import_contracts.py:test_graph_internal_names_every_contract

chunk_findings.detail: The test only requires each name in `CONTRACTS` to appear somewhere in the selected docs row, not that the row names exactly those contracts. For example, a row such as `.importlinter (7 contracts: layers, surfaces-through-api, subprocess-home, fsio-home, digest-home, http-home, extras-one-adapter, stale-contract)` satisfies both the name-membership assertions and the `7 contracts` substring assertion, even though the documentation has drifted by listing an extra contract.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_architecture_import_contracts.py:test_graph_internal_names_every_contract

chunk_findings.detail: The added test does not reliably validate the documented contract count. It partitions on the first literal `contracts:` and then discards everything after the first `)`, so the count can be either swallowed into the first parsed name or ignored entirely. For example, if the documentation row is written in the natural form implied by the bug, `Import-linter contracts: 7 contracts: home, fsio-home, http-home)`, then `after` becomes ` 7 contracts: home, fsio-home, http-home)` and the first parsed “name” is `7 contracts: home`, so the test fails even though every contract is listed. Conversely, if the row is `Import-linter contracts: home, fsio-home, http-home) (6 contracts)`, the split on `)` stops before the stale count and `named == set(CONTRACTS)` passes, so the test does not catch the count drift it was intended to guard.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_architecture_import_contracts.py:test_graph_internal_names_every_contract

chunk_findings.detail: The new parser splits on the first `"contracts:"` in the row, which is the literal label `Import-linter contracts:`, not the delimiter before the contract list. For the row this change fixes, e.g. `Import-linter contracts: 7 contracts: http-home, http, ...`, `row.partition("contracts:")` leaves `after` as `" 7 contracts: http-home, http, ..."`; the subsequent comma split then yields `"7 contracts: http-home"` as a contract name. `named` therefore never equals `set(CONTRACTS)`, so the regression test fails even when the documentation is correct.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_architecture_import_contracts.py:test_graph_internal_names_every_contract
